title: Implement watermark-based metering for intermittent streaming sessions
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Background:

We frequently see customer complaints and internal audit mismatches for streaming sessions that: clients pause/resume connections, networks drop frames, or client-side retries resend fragments. Current token accounting heuristics (finalize-on-close plus fragment de-dup) fail to consistently attribute input vs. output tokens when sessions are intermittent, leading to overcharging, undercharging, or ambiguous provisional credit states.

Problem statement:

We need a robust, eventually-consistent metering approach for streaming sessions that: (1) provides near-real-time provisional balances for rate-limiting decisions, (2) produces deterministic final invoices for billing, and (3) tolerates reordered/duplicated fragments and multi-path delivery (e.g., reconnects to different frontend). Existing approaches either finalize too early (over-credits) or hold tokens indefinitely (blocking quotas).

This ticket proposes a watermark-based metering pipeline that assigns stable attributions to tokens using monotonically-increasing watermarks per session + durable checkpoints in the metering stream. The watermark drives provisional credit windows, reconciliation, and finalization semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Define a session watermark protocol that survives reconnects and frontend failover
Implement provisional_credit ledger entries keyed by (session_id, watermark) with idempotency token
Rate limiter consults provisional credits and enforces guarantees without double-counting on reconnects
Reconciliation job finalizes or reclaims provisional credits within SLA (configurable; default 5 minutes)
Integration test coverage for: out-of-order fragments, duplicate fragments, midstream model-switch fallback, client resume from earlier watermark
Audit log exposes mapping from watermark -> tokens_in -> tokens_out for billing reconciliation
design_notes:
High-level design:

1) Watermark semantics:
   - Every streaming session is assigned a monotonic watermark counter W (uint64) stored in the session metadata store. Clients / frontends attach a per-fragment watermark that must be >= current session watermark. On reconnect, the client may resume using the last-known watermark; frontends reconcile with the session metadata to avoid regressions.

2) Provisional credits ledger:
   - For each watermark W we write a provisional credit record: (session_id, W, tokens_input, tokens_output_estimate, idempotency_key, status=provisional, created_at).
   - Provisional records are compact and chosen such that their lifespan is short (default 5 minutes). They are used by rate limiters and quota checks.

3) Durable checkpoints and finalization:
   - A periodic checkpoint daemon (reconciler) consumes the ordered stream of provisional records per session and produces final billing events when it detects session quiescence or explicit client close. Finalization rules:
     a) If no new watermark > W is seen for the session within finalize_window, finalize W as-is.
     b) If later watermarks arrive that overlap tokens with W, the reconciler deduplicates using idempotency_key + token-offset map.

4) Handling duplicates & reordering:
   - Each fragment carries an offset range (input_token_start, input_token_end) and an idempotency_key. Provisional records include the observed ranges; dedupe logic merges overlapping ranges deterministically (favor earliest observed fragment for attribution).

5) Rate limiting interactions:
   - The rate limiter consumes the sum of finalized credits + sum of provisional credits where provisional.age < provisional_ttl and provisional.status == provisional. When provisional credits are reclaimed on reconciliation, we emit corrective metrics and (if necessary) soft-throttle signals to downstream consumer quota metrics to avoid immediate user impact.

Operational knobs and config:
   - provisional_ttl: how long a provisional record is trusted for RL (default 5m)
   - finalize_window: idle window to finalize a watermark (default 30s)
   - reconciliation_batch_size: controls throughput and memory footprint

Durability & recovery:
   - Session watermark and provisional ledger are stored in the durable metering store (same S3+WAL-backed service used by billing pipeline). On migration/upgrade, WAL replay restores last watermark and provisional rows.
implementation_steps: Add watermark counter and last_seen_watermark to session metadata schema (DB migration)
Extend streaming frame envelope to include watermark, token offset range, and idempotency_key (protocol change + SDK patch)
Implement provisional credits API: write_provisional(session_id, watermark, payload) and read_provisionals(session_id)
Integrate provisional read into existing rate limiter lookup path (ensure low-latency reads via local cache)
Build reconciler service: consume per-session provisionals, run finalization/dedupe, emit final billing events to ledger
Add reconciliation metrics and tracing hooks; wire to Console dashboards and rollouts for canary testing
Add end-to-end tests in integration harness and fuzz tests for reordering/duplicates
Coordinate SDK release and frontend change during a staged roll-out (canary frontends -> all regions)
test_plan: Unit tests for watermark increment semantics and DB migration (simulate race reconcilers)
Property-based tests: random reorder/duplicate fragments; assert final token totals deterministic vs. golden model
Integration tests: client reconnect to different frontend with resumed watermark, assert no double-charge and quotas enforced
Load test: high fanout sessions with provisional_ttl=5m to validate reconciler memory & latency
Billing reconciliation e2e: create synthetic sessions that exercise reclaim flow and verify refund/correction emits
rollout_plan: Staged rollout: 1) Deploy DB migration and provisional API behind feature flag. 2) Launch reconciler in non-authoritative mode (read-only observability) for 48h to validate detection heuristics. 3) Enable provisional read for rate-limiter in canary region and monitor console metrics for anomalies. 4) Enable full finalization and billing emission incrementally region-by-region. 5) After 2 days of stable canary, flip global flag and deprecate legacy heuristics.
risks: Increased read latency for rate limiter if provisional lookups are not cached
Edge-case double-count if idempotency keys collide or clients misbehave
Provisional_ttl misconfiguration might cause temporary under-enforcement of quotas
Reconciler bug could reclaim legitimate provisional credits leading to refunds and customer confusion
notes: Related follow-ups: post-launch we should evaluate shrinking provisional_ttl for low-latency interactive apps and add a customer-visible 'provisional_balance' field in the Console and SDKs. Also consider moving idempotency key generation client-side for stronger attributions.
audit_log_requirements: Every provisional -> final transition must emit a compact audit record: (session_id, watermark, provisional_tokens, final_tokens, reconciler_id, reconciliation_time, dedupe_rows) that is retained for 365 days.
communication_plan: Notify affected customers via in-product banner during rollout with guidance on SDK versions. Coordinate with Support and CS; prepare FAQ covering possible short-term billing corrections and how to request manual review.
estimated_impact: Reduce streaming billing variance by ~85% for intermittent sessions; expected cut in customer disputes related to streaming token counts. Slight increase in metering storage (provisional rows) estimated at +3% storage cost in first month.
